title: Rao Shiv Bahadur Singh v. State of Vindhya Pradesh

content.caseIdentity: Rao Shiv Bahadur Singh v. State of Vindhya Pradesh, (1953) SCR 1188
content.facts: The appellants were prosecuted for offences under the Vindhya Pradesh Ordinance committed prior to the commencement of the Constitution of India, and challenged the procedure of trial as violating Article 20(1).
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether Article 20(1) of the Constitution prohibits changes in criminal procedure or the forum of trial for offences committed prior to the amendment.
content.ratioDecidendi: Article 20(1) prohibits convictions and penalties under ex post facto laws; it does NOT prohibit changes in procedure or the forum of trial. A person accused of an offence has no vested right in a particular course of procedure or in being tried by a specific court, provided the procedure applied does not amount to an ex post facto enhancement of penalty or deprivation of fair trial.
content.holding: Upheld the application of new procedural rules to the trial of offences committed prior to the procedural amendment.
content.relevance: The authoritative constitutional benchmark establishing that BNSS procedure can lawfully govern new investigations of pre-July 2024 offences without infringing Article 20(1).
